domain_symbols.state_space: linear state, input, and output spaces

rules.name: Linear state-space model rule
rules.input_form: x' = Ax + Bu and y = Cx + Du
preconditions: State, input, and output dimensions are fixed
rules.operation: Represent a controlled linear system in standard state-space form.
examples: Control input enters dynamics through the input matrix B in state-space form
counterexamples: Suppressing the input channel while still calling the model controlled is invalid

rules.name: Controllability matrix criterion seed
rules.input_form: pair (A,B)
preconditions: The system is finite-dimensional, linear, and time-invariant
rules.operation: Test controllability by the rank of the classical controllability matrix.
examples: Repeated action of A on the input directions tests state reachability
counterexamples: Checking only the rank of B is insufficient in general

rules.name: Observability matrix criterion seed
rules.input_form: pair (A,C)
preconditions: The system is finite-dimensional, linear, and time-invariant
rules.operation: Test observability by the rank of the classical observability matrix.
examples: Repeated output sampling through powers of A tests recoverability of the internal state
counterexamples: Measuring one output snapshot alone is insufficient in general

rules.name: Lyapunov stability matrix seed
rules.input_form: linear system x' = Ax
preconditions: The system matrix and a symmetric candidate certificate are fixed
rules.operation: Certify linear asymptotic stability through a quadratic Lyapunov condition.
examples: Quadratic Lyapunov functions certify decay of linear autonomous systems under the standard hypotheses
counterexamples: Using an indefinite quadratic form as a Lyapunov certificate is invalid

rules.name: Linear quadratic regulator objective seed
rules.input_form: linear dynamics with quadratic state and control penalties
preconditions: State and control weighting structure is fixed
rules.operation: Formulate the standard linear-quadratic regulator problem.
examples: Quadratic penalties balance state regulation against control effort in classical optimal control
counterexamples: Replacing the quadratic objective by an arbitrary nonsmooth cost without changing the method is invalid

rules.name: State feedback pole placement seed
rules.input_form: controllable linear system and desired closed-loop spectrum
preconditions: The standard controllability and admissible spectrum hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Place the closed-loop poles by linear state feedback in the classical controllable setting.
examples: Feedback changes the closed-loop dynamics matrix from A to A - BK
counterexamples: Prescribing arbitrary closed-loop poles for an uncontrollable system is invalid

rules.name: Algebraic Riccati equation seed
rules.input_form: linear-quadratic regulator problem data
preconditions: An LQR weighting structure and stabilizability assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Reduce quadratic optimal control to the algebraic Riccati equation.
examples: Optimal feedback gain can be recovered from a matrix equation instead of by trajectory-level search alone
counterexamples: Arbitrary matrix equations with no quadratic optimal-control origin are not automatically Riccati characterizations

rules.name: Kalman filter seed
rules.input_form: linear Gaussian state model with noisy observations
preconditions: A linear state model, observation model, and Gaussian noise assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Estimate latent state through standard Kalman predictor-corrector updates.
examples: Noisy measurement streams can reconstruct latent state by balancing model prediction against observation residuals
counterexamples: Applying Kalman updates outside the required linear-Gaussian framework without adjustment is invalid

rules.name: Separation principle seed
rules.input_form: linear-quadratic-Gaussian control architecture
rules.output_form: decoupled estimation and control design structure
preconditions: The standard LQG assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Separate controller design and state estimation under standard linear-quadratic-Gaussian hypotheses.
examples: Optimal feedback and optimal filtering can be designed modularly before being combined into one control architecture
counterexamples: Arbitrary nonlinear partially observed control problems do not automatically satisfy the separation principle

rules.name: Model predictive control seed
rules.input_form: finite-horizon constrained control problem
preconditions: A predictive model, constraints, and finite-horizon objective are fixed
rules.operation: Apply repeated finite-horizon constrained optimization in receding-horizon form.
examples: State and input constraints can be handled online by repeated finite-horizon optimization rather than by one offline feedback law only
counterexamples: Choosing a one-shot open-loop plan with no receding-horizon update is not automatically MPC

rules.name: Controllability Gramian seed
rules.input_form: stable linear system with input matrix
preconditions: A stable linear system and reachability-energy setting are fixed
rules.operation: Encode reachability energy and controllability geometry through the controllability Gramian.
examples: Low-energy reachable directions are identified through Gramian geometry rather than through rank tests alone
counterexamples: Using a rank-only criterion as though it already measured control energy is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
